description: Convert a Roman numeral string (uppercase letters I, V, X, L, C, D, M) to its integer value using standard subtractive notation. Return 0 for the empty string. Assume the input is otherwise a well-formed numeral.

Return the Pisano period π(m): the smallest positive k such that the Fibonacci sequence F(0), F(1), ... taken modulo m repeats with period k (i.e. F(k) mod m == 0 and F(k+1) mod m == 1). Assume m >= 1; return 1 for m = 1.

Given a dict mapping string keys to integer values, return a new dict mapping each distinct value (as a string) to a sorted list of the keys that had that value. Use the string form of the integer as the output key. An empty input returns an empty dict.

signature: def top_k_by_value(scores: dict, k: int) -> list:
description: Given a dict mapping string names to integer scores and a non-negative integer k, return a list of the names of the k highest-scoring entries, ordered from highest score to lowest. Ties in score are broken alphabetically by name ascending. If k exceeds the number of entries, return all names in that order; if k is 0, return an empty list.

signature: def minimal_cover_size(universe: list, subsets: list) -> int:
description: Return the minimum number of subsets (from the list of lists subsets) whose union covers every element of universe. Return -1 if the universe cannot be fully covered. Return 0 if universe is empty. Brute-force search over combinations is acceptable for small inputs.

Given a list of strings, return the first string that has already appeared earlier in the list (the first element whose second occurrence comes soonest). Return an empty string if all elements are distinct or the list is empty.

Split sentence on single spaces, reverse the order of the words, and join them back with single spaces. Any trailing punctuation character (one of . ! ?) that ends a word must stay attached to the last position of the word it ends, i.e. punctuation is moved with the word it belongs to only when it terminates the entire sentence; treat the final character of the sentence if it is . ! or ? as sentence-final and keep it at the end of the output, otherwise treat all characters as ordinary. Leading/trailing spaces are ignored; consecutive spaces produce no empty words.

Count the whitespace-separated tokens that are palindromes after lowercasing and removing every non-alphanumeric character. A token that becomes empty after cleaning (e.g. '---') does not count. Single-character palindromes like 'a' do count.

args: Was it a car or a cat I saw

description: Apply the Collatz map (n even -> n//2, n odd -> 3n+1) starting at start until reaching 1. Return a dict with str keys 'steps' (number of applications needed to reach 1) and 'peak' (the maximum value encountered in the sequence, including start). For start <= 0 return {'steps': 0, 'peak': 0}.
Return the length of the longest contiguous run of identical characters in s. For an empty string return 0.
Given a list of weekday indices (0 = Monday ... 6 = Sunday) representing the weekday on which the 13th of each month falls, return how many of them are Fridays (index 4). Return 0 for an empty list.
reference:
def count_fridays_thirteenth_in_cycle(weekdays_of_thirteenths: list) -> int:
    return sum(1 for d in weekdays_of_thirteenths if d == 4)

signature: def intersect_interval_lists(first: list, second: list) -> list:
description: Each argument is a list of closed integer intervals [lo, hi] (lo <= hi), sorted by lo and pairwise non-overlapping within the same list. Return the list of intervals that lie in both inputs, in sorted order, with no overlap or touching merged. An interval that is a single point (lo == hi) is kept.

signature: def fiscal_quarter(month: int, day: int, fy_start_month: int) -> int:
description: Given a calendar month (1-12) and day, and a fiscal year that begins on the first day of fy_start_month (1-12), return the fiscal quarter number 1-4 that the date falls in. Quarter 1 starts on the first day of fy_start_month, and each quarter spans three consecutive months. The day argument is valid for the month and does not affect the result.

Given a string of digits, return the next term of the look-and-say sequence: consecutive runs of identical digits are replaced by the run length followed by the digit. An empty string returns an empty string.

Each string contains exactly one run of decimal digits (e.g. 'file12.txt'). Sort the strings by the integer value of that digit run ascending; ties keep original order. Return a new list. Assume every input string contains at least one digit.

Separate the integers into evens and odds, each keeping original relative order. Output alternates starting with an even, taking one from each group in turn; when one group runs out, append the remainder of the other group in order. Zero counts as even. Negative numbers are classified by Python's % 2 (so -3 is odd).

signature: def partition_by_membership(items: list, members: list) -> dict:
description: Split items into two lists according to whether each item is in members. Return a dict with keys "in" and "out", each mapping to the items (preserving original order and duplicates) that are respectively present in or absent from members.

Given an integer n in the range 0 to 255 inclusive, return the integer obtained by reversing the order of its 8 bits (bit 0 becomes bit 7, bit 1 becomes bit 6, and so on). Leading zeros count as bits, so reverse_bits_8(1) is 128.

Parse a version string of the form 'MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH' optionally prefixed with 'v' and optionally followed by a '-' pre-release suffix, returning [major, minor, patch] as ints. The pre-release suffix is discarded. Missing MINOR or PATCH default to 0 (so 'v2' gives [2, 0, 0]). Build metadata after '+' is also discarded.

signature: def days_between_dates(y1: int, m1: int, d1: int, y2: int, m2: int, d2: int) -> int:
description: Return the number of days from the first date to the second date (second minus first), as a signed integer. Dates are proleptic Gregorian and valid. The result is 0 when the dates are equal and negative when the second date is earlier.

Peel the grid into concentric rings from the outside in (ring 0 is the outer border, ring 1 the border of the remaining inner rectangle, and so on). Return a list where element i is the sum of all values in ring i. Works for non-square grids; an empty grid returns an empty list.

Return a dict mapping each integer k in 1..limit (as a string key, e.g. "12") to the sum of its proper divisors (divisors strictly less than k). For k = 1 the sum is 0. Return an empty dict if limit < 1.

Parse a duration such as '1h30m15s' into total seconds. Each component is a non-negative integer followed by one of the units h, m, s; components may appear in any subset but must be in descending unit order (h before m before s) and each unit at most once. Return -1 if the string is malformed or empty.
Return the character that appears most often in s. Ties are broken by returning the character that appears first in s. If s is empty, return an empty string.

Grid cells are 0 (open) or 1 (wall). Find the minimum number of 4-directional moves from top-left (0,0) to bottom-right to move between open cells; return -1 if no path exists or if either start or end cell is a wall. A 1x1 open grid returns 0. Empty grid returns -1.

Given a list of [start, end] integer pairs (inclusive, start <= end), merge any windows that overlap or touch (i.e. share at least one integer or are adjacent such that end + 1 == next start). Return the merged windows as a list of [start, end] lists sorted by start. An empty input returns an empty list.

Expand a comma-separated list of integers and inclusive ranges like '3-6' into a sorted list of unique ints. Negative numbers are not used in the spec; whitespace around items is ignored. If a range's start is greater than its end, it contributes nothing.

Given a non-empty rectangular matrix (list of equal-length lists of ints) and a valid column index col, return a new matrix whose rows are sorted by the value in column col ascending. Rows with equal value in that column are ordered by their row sum ascending, then keep original order if still tied. The input must not be mutated.
reference:
def sort_matrix_rows_by_column_then_row_sum(matrix: list, col: int) -> list:
    return [list(r) for r in sorted(matrix, key=lambda r: (r[col], sum(r)))]

signature: def count_days_covered(ranges: list, window_start: int, window_end: int) -> int:
description: Each element of ranges is a [lo, hi] inclusive integer pair (possibly lo > hi, in which case it is empty and contributes nothing). Return the number of distinct integers within the closed window [window_start, window_end] that are covered by at least one range; return 0 if window_start > window_end.

Return the most frequent word in text, lowercased. Words are maximal runs of letters and apostrophes-free ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z). On ties, return the word that appears first in the text. Return an empty string if there are no words.

args: x y z z y x x

signature: def longest_strictly_rising_window(xs: list, width: int) -> int:
description: Among all contiguous windows of exactly length width, count how many are strictly increasing (each element greater than the previous) and return that count. If width is less than 1 or greater than len(xs), return 0. Result is a count, not a maximum.

Consider Pascal's triangle with row 0 being [1]. Return 'odd' if the number of odd entries in the given row (0-indexed) is odd, otherwise return 'even'. Negative rows return 'invalid'. The count of odd entries in row r equals 2 raised to the number of 1-bits in r.

signature: def spiral_order_fill(rows: int, cols: int) -> list:
description: Return a rows x cols grid (as a list of lists) filled with 1, 2, 3, ... in clockwise spiral order starting at the top-left corner. If rows or cols is 0, return an empty list.

Given a list of non-empty lists treated as sets, return the minimum size of a set H such that H intersects every input set. Use brute force over subsets of the union of all elements. If the input list is empty, return 0.
Return the number of integers k with 1 <= k <= n such that gcd(k, n) == 1, i.e. Euler's totient of n. For n = 1 the result is 1. Assume n >= 1.

Each interval is a two-element list [start, end] of integers with start <= end. Sort the intervals by length (end - start) ascending, ties broken by start ascending. Return a new list of the same inner lists; the input must not be mutated.
reference:
def sort_intervals_by_length_then_start(intervals: list) -> list:
    return sorted(intervals, key=lambda iv: (iv[1] - iv[0], iv[0]))

description: Given a list of integers, partition it into maximal runs where each element is exactly one greater than the previous (consecutive increasing by 1). Return a list of strings, one per run, formatted as 'a-b' when the run has length >= 2 and 'a' when it has length 1, where a is the first value and b the last. An empty input returns an empty list.

Parse a string of semicolon-separated key=value pairs into a dict. Whitespace around keys and values is stripped. Empty segments (e.g. from leading, trailing, or doubled semicolons) are ignored. If a key appears more than once, the last value wins. Segments without '=' are ignored.

signature: def count_common_elements(a: list, b: list) -> int:
description: Return the number of distinct values that appear in both lists a and b. Duplicates within a list count once. Lists may be empty, in which case the result is 0.
reference:
def count_common_elements(a, b):
    return len(set(a) & set(b))

description: Return a dict mapping each adjacent two-character substring of s to the number of times it occurs (overlapping occurrences count). Keys are the 2-character strings. If s has fewer than 2 characters, return an empty dict.

signature: def largest_gap_between_points(points: list, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
description: Given a list of integer points (possibly unsorted, possibly with duplicates or points outside [lo, hi]) on the closed interval [lo, hi], return the length of the largest gap between consecutive boundary-inclusive points, where the boundaries lo and hi are always included. Points outside [lo, hi] are ignored. If lo > hi, return 0.

Return the elements of a rectangular 2D list in clockwise spiral order starting at the top-left corner. An empty grid returns []. Works for any rectangular shape including single rows and single columns.

Each item is a string. Strings consisting only of ASCII digits are converted to int and summed with adjacent digit-string items that are also numeric, forming maximal consecutive numeric blocks; each block becomes a single int equal to the sum. Non-numeric strings (including empty strings) pass through unchanged. Empty input returns an empty list.

Consider the main diagonal cells grid[i][i] for i from 0 up to min(rows, cols)-1. Return the string that appears most often among those cells. On a tie, return the lexicographically smallest tied string. If the grid is empty, return an empty string.
Given a list of string labels, return the label occurring strictly more than half the time. If no label is a strict majority (including for an empty list), return the string "none".

Parse a string of semicolon-separated 'key=value' pairs into a dict. Whitespace around keys and values is stripped. Empty segments (e.g. from consecutive or trailing semicolons) are ignored. If a segment has no '=', it is ignored; if a key appears more than once, the last occurrence wins.

signature: def clamp_ranges_to_bounds(ranges: list, lo: int, hi: int) -> list:
description: Given a list of closed integer ranges [a, b] and bounds lo, hi, clip each range to [lo, hi]. Drop any range that lies entirely outside the bounds (including when the intersection is empty). Preserve the input order of the surviving ranges and do not merge them. Return a list of [a, b] lists.

Sort a list of integers so that values appearing more often come first; values with equal frequency are ordered by value ascending. Every occurrence of a value appears contiguously in the output. Return a new list.

For integer n >= 2, find the representation n = b^e with e maximal (e >= 1). Return the list [b, e]. If n = 1 return [1, 1]. Here b is always a positive integer and e is the largest exponent for which an integer root exists.

Convert a CSS hex color into [r, g, b] integers 0-255. Accepts '#RRGGBB' and the shorthand '#RGB' (each digit doubled, so '#f08' is [255, 0, 136]). The leading '#' is required and hex digits may be upper or lower case. Return [-1, -1, -1] for any malformed input (wrong length, non-hex characters, or missing '#').
Given a non-negative integer n, return the length of the longest contiguous block of 1 bits in its binary representation. Return 0 when n is 0.
Return the number of integer points (x, y) satisfying |x| + |y| <= r, i.e. the lattice points inside or on the diamond of Manhattan radius r centered at the origin. Return 0 if r is negative.

Run-length encode the string s as a list of [character, count] pairs, in order of appearance, where each pair is a 2-element list. Consecutive identical characters form one run. An empty string returns an empty list.

Given a 2D list of integers, return the length of the longest contiguous run of zeros that lies within a single row (runs do not wrap across rows). Return 0 if there are no zeros or the grid is empty.

Split a CSV line into fields. Fields are separated by commas. A field wrapped in double quotes may contain commas; within a quoted field, a doubled quote '""' represents a literal quote character. Fields are returned exactly as parsed, without stripping whitespace. An empty line yields a single empty field [''].

signature: def jaccard_percent(a: list, b: list) -> int:
description: Compute the Jaccard similarity of the sets built from a and b, expressed as an integer percentage rounded down (floor). That is floor(100 * |A intersect B| / |A union B|). If both sets are empty, return 100.

Given a list of lists representing sets, return the length of the longest chain S1 < S2 < ... where each set is a strict subset of the next (after deduplicating identical sets). Return 0 for an empty input.

signature: def covering_sets_indices(universe: list, sets: list) -> list:
description: Given a universe list and a list of candidate sets (lists), return the sorted list of indices i such that sets[i] is a superset of the universe. Duplicates in inputs are ignored. If universe is empty, every index qualifies. Returns an empty list if no set covers the universe.
Given a list of strings, return the length of the longest common prefix shared by every string in the list. If the list is empty, return 0. Comparison is case-sensitive.

signature: def day_of_year(year: int, month: int, day: int) -> int:
description: Return the 1-based ordinal day within the year for a proleptic Gregorian date given as year, month (1-12), day. Leap years follow the Gregorian rule (divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400). Inputs are assumed valid.
reference:
def day_of_year(year: int, month: int, day: int) -> int:
    leap = (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0) or year % 400 == 0
    days = [31, 29 if leap else 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31]
    return sum(days[:month - 1]) + day

description: Return the 0-based index of the least significant set bit of a non-negative integer n. If n is 0, return -1. Negative inputs are not allowed; the function may assume n >= 0.

signature: def reverse_base_representation(n: int, base: int) -> int:
description: Write n >= 0 in the given base (2 <= base <= 36), reverse its digit sequence, and return the resulting value as a Python int (interpreted in the same base). For n = 0 return 0. Trailing zeros in the original become leading zeros and are dropped in the result.

Perform run-length encoding: each maximal run of identical consecutive characters is replaced by the character followed by its run length in decimal, but runs of length 1 are written as the character alone. Comparison is case-sensitive and includes spaces. Return an empty string for empty input.

Factor n >= 2 into primes and return a string listing the prime factors in increasing order, joined by '*', with repeated primes written as power notation 'p^e' when the exponent e > 1. For example 12 gives '2^2*3'. Return an empty string if n < 2.

Given a list of integers, return a list of [value, count] pairs describing maximal runs of equal consecutive values, in order. Values equal to 0 are excluded entirely (they break runs but produce no pair). An empty input returns an empty list.

Return the digital root of a non-negative integer n: repeatedly sum its decimal digits until a single digit remains. Digital root of 0 is 0. Negative inputs are not part of the spec and will not be tested.
Return the length of the longest word in the text. Words are maximal runs of ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z); all other characters act as separators. Return 0 if the text contains no letters.

Given a list of log lines of the form '[LEVEL] message', count how many lines carry each level. Return a dict mapping level name to count, with the level string taken exactly as written between brackets. Lines not starting with '[' or lacking a closing ']' are skipped. Matching is case-sensitive; 'warn' and 'WARN' are distinct levels.

Build an uppercase acronym from phrase by taking the first letter of each word. Words are maximal runs of letters and digits; any other character separates them. Words that begin with a digit contribute that digit. Return the empty string if there are no words.

Given a list of integers that is sorted in non-decreasing order and may contain duplicates, return a list of compressed range strings. A maximal block of consecutive integers (each exactly one more than the previous, duplicates ignored) of length 1 becomes str(n); a block of length 2 or more becomes 'a-b' with a the first and b the last value. An empty input returns an empty list.
